title: Evidence upload intent and idempotency-scope supersession (DATA-001-WP2 revision: additive, with one governed constraint relaxation)
status_note: Approved in principle by the sponsor on 2026-10-14. APPROVED FOLLOWING INDEPENDENT REVIEW (Codex final verdict APPROVE, 0 remaining material findings; relaxation P9-S2-ADD-001-REL-01 explicitly approved), recorded in GATE-033. Forward activation recorded by the accepted Phase-6 snapshot revision P6-SNAPSHOT-REV-001 — REMOTE CI + MERGE PENDING. Not applied to the sponsor's database.

resulting_contract.status: EFFECTIVE 0.3.0 = 0.2.0 + P9-S2-ADD-001 (APPROVED FOLLOWING INDEPENDENT REVIEW, GATE-033; ACTIVATED by P6-SNAPSHOT-REV-001 — REMOTE CI + MERGE PENDING)

api_impact: NONE. API-001/OAS-001 operations, DTOs, states and status codes are unchanged; client_declared_sha256 stays optional.
reasons: evidence_item.content_sha256 and byte_length are NOT NULL, but API-001 §12 creates the evidence item before any bytes exist and the authoritative digest is computed only at PUT; display_filename and declared_byte_length have no column.

api_idempotency_record makes its scope columns write-once and uq_api_idempotency_scope covers the full scope with no expiry term, so the OPS-001 §5 'fresh claim after active_until' is impossible without deleting a governed record, which tl_app_runtime cannot and should not do.

byte_definitions.TL_EVIDENCE_BYTES_V1: The exact HTTP request body bytes of putEvidenceContent, with no decoding, normalisation, trimming or newline conversion. content_sha256 is SHA-256 over exactly these bytes.

evidence_upload_intent_state.note: OPEN until the first accepted PUT creates the evidence_item; MATERIALIZED is terminal for the intent.

evidence_put_rejection_category.note: Most recent rejected PUT, recorded without changing the intent state; the client may retry with the exact declared bytes.

tables_added.name: evidence_upload_intent
tables_added.purpose: P9-S2-ADD-001: durable record of an accepted createEvidenceUpload before its bytes exist (pre-content intake stage of DATA-001 EvidenceItem). Its identifier IS the API evidence_id and, once the first accepted PUT materializes it, the evidence_item_id. Holds declared values only; never a digest the server has not computed.

columns.name: evidence_upload_intent_id
columns.description: API evidence_id (application-generated UUIDv4); equals evidence_item_id after materialization.

columns.name: initiated_by_principal_id
columns.description: Authenticated principal that initiated the upload (server-derived).

columns.name: declared_byte_length
columns.description: Declared byte length; the PUT body must match exactly.

columns.name: display_filename
columns.description: Untrusted display name; never a storage path or download filename.

columns.name: client_declared_sha256
columns.description: Advisory client digest (optional, API-001); a mismatch with the server-computed digest is rejected and recorded. Never authoritative.

columns.name: idempotency_key
columns.description: Internal key shared with the EVIDENCE_INGEST cross_store_operation and the evidence_item (not the client Idempotency-Key).

columns.name: last_rejection_category
columns.description: Category of the most recent rejected PUT.

unique.name: uq_evidence_upload_intent_idempotency
unique.purpose: One intent per internal ingest key, shared 1:1 with its EVIDENCE_INGEST cross_store_operation and evidence_item.

unique.name: uq_evidence_upload_intent_evidence_item
unique.purpose: An evidence item is materialized from at most one intent; also the supporting index for the evidence_item FK (DC-24).

checks.name: ck_evidence_upload_intent_materialized
checks.purpose: MATERIALIZED exactly when the evidence item exists (no half-materialized intent).

checks.name: ck_evidence_upload_intent_same_identity
checks.rule: evidence_item_id IS NULL OR evidence_item_id = evidence_upload_intent_id
checks.purpose: The API evidence_id is one identity across intent and evidence_item.

checks.name: ck_evidence_upload_intent_declared_length
checks.purpose: Declared length is a non-negative byte count (the request validator requires >= 1).

checks.name: ck_evidence_upload_intent_bounded_text
checks.rule: length(declared_media_type) <= 255 AND (display_filename IS NULL OR length(display_filename) <= 255)

indexes.name: ix_evidence_upload_intent_submission
indexes.justification: listEvidence by submission in created order, and deletion enumeration for the submission FK (DC-24).

indexes.name: ix_evidence_upload_intent_open
indexes.justification: Reconciliation of abandoned uploads (no automatic cleanup period; UX-002#5 / OI-05).

transition_guards: intent_state OPEN -> MATERIALIZED only, in the same transaction that inserts the evidence_item with the same identifier; MATERIALIZED is terminal for the intent.

constraint_triggers.name: tg_evidence_upload_intent_guard
constraint_triggers.rule: Declared values, identity, idempotency_key, created_at and retention reference are immutable; intent_state moves only OPEN -> MATERIALIZED; evidence_item_id is write-once.
constraint_triggers.purpose: Keeps the intake record an accountable, append-style history of what was declared.

tables_amended.name: api_idempotency_record

columns_added.name: superseded_at
columns_added.description: Write-once: set only after active_until has passed, when a reused key starts a fresh claim (OPS-001 §5). The superseded record is kept, never deleted.

from.name: uq_api_idempotency_scope
from.purpose: Atomic claim: exactly one record per principal + operation + target resource + key; concurrent duplicates conflict on this constraint instead of check-then-insert.

to.name: uq_api_idempotency_scope
to.purpose: Atomic claim: at most one GOVERNING (non-superseded) record per principal + operation + target resource + key; concurrent duplicates conflict on this partial unique index instead of check-then-insert. Superseded history is kept, never deleted.

transition_guards_replaced.from: Claim = INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (uq_api_idempotency_scope) DO NOTHING with execution_state IN_PROGRESS and a fresh claim_token; only the inserting request executes.
transition_guards_replaced.to: Claim = INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against the partial unique index uq_api_idempotency_scope (WHERE superseded_at IS NULL) with execution_state IN_PROGRESS and a fresh claim_token; only the inserting request executes.

transition_guards_replaced.from: After active_until the record no longer governs the key and may be purged by governed retention action; behaviour of a reused key after expiry is the documented expiry policy (OPS-001 §5).
transition_guards_replaced.to: After active_until the record no longer governs the key (OPS-001 §5): a reused key is a NEW request. The expired record is marked superseded_at = now() by compare-and-swap (only while active_until <= now() and superseded_at IS NULL) and a fresh claim is inserted in the same transaction. Superseded records are kept unchanged and never govern again; no record is deleted by the request path.

transition_guards_added: superseded_at is write-once and may move NULL -> value only when active_until <= now(); a superseded record is immutable.

tables_amended.name: cross_store_operation
transition_guards_added: attempt_count is the content-write fencing token: it never decreases and advances by exactly one per attempt; an attempt records its outcome only WHERE attempt_count still equals its own number and state = CONTENT_PENDING, so a stale success or failure changes nothing. While CONTENT_PENDING, next_attempt_not_before is the live attempt lease (approved 30 s); a later attempt may take over only after it passes. No transaction spans the content store.

constraint_relaxations.to: UNIQUE (principal_reference_id, operation_id, target_resource_scope, idempotency_key_digest) WHERE superseded_at IS NULL
constraint_relaxations.why: OPS-001 §5 makes a reused key after active_until a new request. Under the full-scope constraint the only way to admit that request is to delete the governed record, which tl_app_runtime cannot and must not do. Restricting uniqueness to governing (non-superseded) records admits exactly one new claim per scope while keeping the history.
preserved_invariants: At most one governing record per (principal, operation, target resource, key digest) at any instant: the partial unique index still serializes concurrent claims (atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT, never check-then-insert).
Within the 24 h active window behaviour is unchanged: replay, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED and IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS exactly as P6-WP6.
A record can be superseded only after its own active_until, once, by compare-and-swap; a superseded record is immutable and never governs again.
Only the SHA-256 key digest is stored; no raw key, no cached response body, no DELETE grant, no request-path deletion.
Completion stays fenced by claim_token and atomic with the governed effect.
migration_compatibility: Existing 0003 rows all have superseded_at NULL, so they satisfy the partial index exactly as they satisfied the full constraint; the index build cannot fail on them.
Migration 0004 adds the column, drops the constraint and creates the partial unique index (same name) in one migration transaction; there is no window without uniqueness.

Application code on a 0003 database keeps full-scope semantics (an expired key is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, stricter than OPS-001 §5) and evidence intake stays disabled, so mixed versions never execute a request twice.

There is no automatic downgrade: as for 0001-0003, downgrade() raises and a rollback needs its own review. Restoring the full-scope constraint would be lossless only while no record is superseded; afterwards it would require deleting history.
constraint_relaxations.review_required: Accepted explicitly by the independent review recorded in GATE-033 (it was not covered by "additive").

api_resolution.getEvidenceMetadata/listEvidence: Every evidence_id has exactly one evidence_upload_intent. upload_state = map(evidence_item.content_state) via api_upload_state.maps_from when materialized, else AWAITING_CONTENT. content_sha256/byte_length/verified_media_type/finalized_at come only from evidence_item; artifact_kind, declared_media_type, display_filename and ingested_at (= created_at) from the intent.
api_resolution.putEvidenceContent: First accepted PUT: insert evidence_item (RECEIVED, server digest) and set the intent MATERIALIZED in one transaction. Each content-write attempt takes the next attempt_count (fencing token) and a 30 s lease, writes the encrypted object outside any transaction, and records CONTENT_STORED (with the EVIDENCE_STORED audit) or FAILED_RETRYABLE/FAILED_TERMINAL only while it still holds the fence. Identical re-PUT is a no-op on stored content, waits (503 Retry-After) while another attempt holds a live lease, or resumes after it; different bytes -> STATE_CONFLICT.
api_resolution.finalizeEvidence: 202. Re-read, decrypt and verify digest, length and media; INTEGRITY_VERIFIED -> FINALIZED with the custody audit in one transaction; verification failure -> INTEGRITY_FAILED + INTEGRITY_FAILURE audit, never FINALIZED.

tl_app_runtime: SELECT, INSERT on evidence_upload_intent, evidence_item, cross_store_operation
UPDATE(intent_state, last_rejection_category, state_changed_at, evidence_item_id) on evidence_upload_intent
UPDATE(content_state, state_changed_at, ecs_locator, verified_at, finalized_at, verified_media_type) on evidence_item
UPDATE(state, attempt_count, last_failure_category, next_attempt_not_before, state_changed_at, terminal_at, ecs_object_ref) on cross_store_operation
